items.stem: A manager asks 'why did margin fall last quarter?'. Which analytics type does this request call for?

options.rationale: Correct: explaining why something happened is diagnostic.
Descriptive reports what happened, not why.
Predictive forecasts the future, not past causes.
Prescriptive recommends actions, not root causes.

items.explanation: Correct: explaining why something happened is diagnostic.

items.stem: Which TWO practices help ensure a trusted single source of truth for metrics? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Define each metric once in a shared semantic layer
options.rationale: Correct: a central definition prevents divergent calculations.

options.text: Assign each KPI a named business owner
options.rationale: Correct: clear ownership keeps definitions maintained and accountable.

options.text: Let each report author define revenue their own way
options.rationale: Divergent definitions break trust in the numbers.

options.text: Avoid documenting metric formulas so they stay flexible
options.rationale: Undocumented formulas cause inconsistency and disputes.

items.explanation: Correct: a central definition prevents divergent calculations.

items.stem: Why is querying production transactional systems directly for reports usually discouraged?

options.text: It can degrade operational performance and lacks a modelled, consistent reporting structure
options.rationale: Correct: reporting load and unmodelled schemas make direct queries risky.

options.text: Transactional systems contain no useful data
options.rationale: They contain the source data; the issue is how it is accessed.

options.text: Reports can only read from spreadsheets
options.rationale: Reports can read from many modelled sources.

options.text: It is always faster than a warehouse
options.rationale: Direct queries are typically slower and riskier for reporting.

items.explanation: Correct: reporting load and unmodelled schemas make direct queries risky.
